LESSON: SURFACE PREPARATION

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: General
Strand: Wood Processes and Products
Topic 3.3: Surface preparation
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 16

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Surface preparation, part of Wood Processes and Products in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 General.

Key inquiry question: Why is surface preparation in wood finishing important?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Surface preparation together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and collaboration: learner develops speaking, listening and teamwork skills when discussing reasons for

finishing a product.

• Digital Literacy: learner develops digital skills when interacting and manipulating digital devices to search online for

materials required for surface preparation.

• Learning to Learn: learner reflects on their own work when visiting nearby wood workshops to learn the preparation of

wood surface

Values:
• Respect: learner accommodates opinions of others during discussions on materials, tools that are required for surface

preparation.

• Love: learner interact and share tools while carrying out the operations of preparing the surface for wood finishes.

• Responsibility: learner takes care of tools to carry out the preparation of surface for wood finishes.

31

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Environmental conservation: learner manages waste from finishes and surface preparation materials.

Suggested Resources: scraper, sand paper, files, hot iron and cloth, workshop, digital devices, assistive technology, screen

reading software, reliable websites, print media, braille media, varnish, wood

Key Concepts/Skills:

Explaining the reasons for finishing a wood product

Preparing a wood surface to receive clear varnish
